articles.headline: The Book Depository of the African M.E. Church (standing ad) -- address now No. 631 Pine
articles.summary: The Book Depository of the African M.E. Church, No. 631 Pine Street, Philadelphia. Keeps on hand, in connexion with other books, Sabbath School books of various kinds, Question Books, Catechisms Nos. 1, 2 and 3, books generally used in the Public Schools, also stationery, inks, pens, envelopes and blank books. CHANGED: the standing Book Depository ad now prints No. 631 Pine (the General Book Steward's office moved there Nov. 1866); the ad had still read 619 Pine through the spring quarter, so the address is newly updated.

articles.headline: Liberty Hall (notice)
articles.summary: Liberty Hall -- one of the finest halls in the city, situated on Lombard street below 8th, having two large stores on the first floor, two fine basement stores, and a large auditorium on the second floor, 40 by 80 feet, in which lectures, concerts, and fairs are held. Application for the use of the hall may be made to Rev. S. Smith, 921 Lombard street. Dated June 28th.

articles.headline: Notice (wife desertion)
articles.author: J. W. H. Cathcart
articles.summary: Whereas, my wife, Sarah Cathcart, has voluntarily left my bed and board, all persons are hereby forbid harboring or trusting her on my account, as I will pay no debts of her contracting from this date, July 2d, 1867. J. W. H. Cathcart, No. 210 Quince St.

articles.headline: Died (Jacob Hunter; Mary Elizabeth Shelton)
articles.summary: On the 12th of June, Jacob Hunter, late Steward of Lincoln University [Chester County, Pa.], aged 78 years. He was born in the State of Maryland, but removed to Chester County, Pa., when 18 years old, where he became a member of the Fagg's Manor Presbyterian Church the same year; a pious, industrious man, leaving a widow and several children. On the 23d of June, at 8 o'clock, Mary Elizabeth, daughter of Harriet and Isaac Shelton, aged one year and six months (place not stated).
people: deceased; late steward of Lincoln University, aged 78

articles.headline: Married (Barrett-Reddin)
articles.summary: On the 18th of July, Mr. Joseph Barrett, of Dover, Del., to Miss Rachel Reddin, of Chester City, Pa., by Rev. Wm. Murphy.

articles.headline: Obituaries (Lydia Lane; Wm. Reeves)
articles.summary: Departed this life June 20, 1867, in the triumphs of faith, Sister Lydia Lane, in her 9[5]th year, at Brooklyn, Ill., mother of the well-known Sister Priscilla of Baltimore (signed W. R. R., St. Louis, July 18 -- non-Philadelphia). July 17th, 1867, in the hope of a blissful immortality, Wm. Reeves, aged 16 years (no place of death stated).
people: deceased, aged 16 (place of death not stated)

articles.headline: Notice ('Shall I Call?') -- minister returning North, Philadelphia address 1081 Warnock St
articles.author: R. P. [surname uncertain]
articles.summary: A minister writing from Savannah, Ga. (July 18), intends to return North in a few days and to visit his brother ministers and assist their meetings, asking that replies be sent to him at 1081 Warnock street, Philadelphia (he leaves the South July 27th). He reports that the people in Savannah, under the management of Rev. Anthony L. Stanford, have begun erecting a new church but have not been able to complete it, and references letters from Rev. R. H. Cain of Charleston, S.C., and Rev. T. G. Steward. Signed R. P. [G---].
people: managing the erection of a new church at Savannah (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Cape May
articles.author: Wm. Whipper
articles.summary: A letter from Cape May on the summer season at the resort: large delegations present from Washington, Baltimore, Philadelphia and elsewhere, and a brilliant and successful lecture by Miss Fanny H. Jackson on the popular subject of 'Suffrage,' warmly received. The writer closes with reflections on distinguished colored representatives -- in literature and science a Wheatley, a Fuller and a Banneker (Maryland); in theology a Coker, a Pennington and a Douglass; in oratory a Douglass, a Ward, a Garnet and a Harper -- and names Fanny M. Jackson as the District of Columbia's distinguished representative in science and oratory. Signed Wm. Whipper. (Fanny H./M. Jackson = Fanny Jackson, principal of the Institute for Colored Youth; Wm. Whipper = the abolitionist and lumber merchant.)
people: delivered a lecture on 'Suffrage' at Cape May (Miss; = Fanny M. Jackson, principal of the Institute for Colored Youth)

articles.headline: From Cape Island (letter)
articles.author: Sea Side (pseud.)
articles.summary: At this place the season is backward, both as to people and weather. Reports on the Cape Island (Cape May, N.J.) summer resort season; notes the 'Banneker' House. Rev. Stephen Smith has induced resident Christians to repair the temple of worship. Miss Fanny Jackson, Principal of the Female Department of the Institute for Colored Youth, is stopping at the residence of Rev. Stephen Smith; she lectured Tuesday evening, July 23d, introduced by Sam'l Whipper, Esq. Dated July 24, 1867.
people: Principal, Female Dept., Institute for Colored Youth (Miss); lectured at Cape Island

articles.headline: Letter (reply to Rev. T. Gould on camp-meetings / the A.M.E. Union Camp)
articles.author: D. P. Seaton
articles.summary: Replies to Rev. T. Gould's communication of August 3d about camp-meetings, especially the A.M.E. Union Camp; notes Gould was present at the preacher's meeting in Philadelphia where the matter was discussed. Defends the Union Camp as held for the glory of God. Signed D. P. Seaton, Frankford, Phila.

articles.headline: Let every preacher in the A.M.E. Church read this again and again (Book Concern $7000 appeal)
articles.summary: Editorial appeal to raise $7000 by mid-September or Oct 1 to pay off the Book Concern debt. Names District Book Stewards: Dr. W. T. Revels (Missouri), W. C. Trevan (Indiana), John Turner (Louisiana), Samuel Watts (Ohio), William D. W. Schureman (Baltimore), Denton Dorrell (Philadelphia Conference), Henry Davis (New York), John W. Earley (New England), R. H. Cain (S. Carolina), H. M. Turner (Georgia), Thomas M. D. Ward (California), G. T. Watkins (Virginia). The Book Committee met July 1st and apportioned the $7000 (total $7025): Philadelphia District $1000. Elisha Weaver pledges $100.

articles.headline: Report of Committee on Aid for the Book Concern ($7,000 must be raised)
articles.summary: Committee report, by order of the Conference, proposing a plan to liquidate the Book Concern's debt: each pastor to assess his charge, funds sent by express to Rev. Elisha Weaver, Box 2975, Philadelphia. Signed E. Weaver, Chairman; Stephen Smith, Treasurer; H. J. Rhodes, Secretary; J. M. Williams, J. Mitchell, Wm. Moore.

articles.headline: Notice -- agent appointed for the new Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church

articles.author: J. B. Hamilton

July 25th, 1867.

articles.headline: Deaths (Philadelphia)
articles.summary: Brother Benjamin Bell, one of the oldest members and class-leaders of Bethel church, expired very suddenly last Sabbath; he went to church twice that day, sat down on his door-step on reaching home and died in a few moments. Also: at Frankford, Pa., July 7th, 1867, Elizabeth S. ('Lizzie'), infant daughter of George and Elizabeth Pleasant, aged 9 months, 2 weeks and 1 day.
people: deceased; oldest member and class-leader, Bethel church

articles.summary: FREEDMAN'S CHEAP STORE, [P.?] between 4th and 5th Streets, Beaufort, S.C. articles.summary: An elegant and easy system for cutting and fitting ladies' and children's clothing can be learned in half an hour, at 756 South Eighth Street, below Fitzwater. Agents wanted. Dated aug3-1m (no proprietor named). Repeats Aug 17.

articles.headline: How We Spent Last Sabbath (editor's visit to the Home for Aged and to Camden)
articles.summary: At half past ten o'clock we preached at the Old Folks' Home; sorry to find Mother Boggs and a number of the others much indisposed. In the afternoon we went over to Camden, New Jersey, to assist Brother Hamilton in the administration of the Lord's Supper; the congregation much increased, and expected to come up strongly for the $7025.

articles.summary: The Board of Managers of the Home for Aged and Infirm Colored Persons is in great need of funds. Contributions may be left with the matron at the Home, or with Samuel R. articles.headline: Death of Robert Harris -- Union A.M.E. Church resolutions and funeral
articles.summary: Resolutions of the quarterly meeting conference of the Union A.M.E. church (Philadelphia) on the death of Brother Robert Harris, who departed this life after a protracted illness in July 1867 in the city of Philadelphia. He had been a member of the church about twenty-seven years, a class leader and trustee. His Masonic brethren of Eastern Star Lodge, No. 19 (printed), and the members of the church proceeded from his late residence to the church, where Rev. Wm. Moore, elder in charge, delivered a discourse; the funeral cortege proceeded to Olive Cemetery. Committee: Edward Young, Albert H. Hall, Jas. E. Turner; Wm. Moore, Elder in Charge.

articles.headline: Notes by the Way, No. I (Trip to Wilmington, N.C.)
articles.author: J. M. Brown
articles.summary: Travel letter: left Baltimore Friday July 26th on the Bay Line steamer Geo. Leary to Norfolk, then to Wilmington, N.C. (Rev. Samuel B. Williams, pastor), then Halifax N.C. and Richmond. Reports at length on Mrs. Frances Ellen Watkins Harper, who addressed the colored Baptist and Methodist Sabbath-schools at Wilmington and lectured to some 2000 persons; at Richmond she addressed the people in the House of Delegates of Virginia ('Mrs. Harper in the capital of Virginia'). Visited an orphan asylum near Wilmington (American Missionary Association; matron Mrs. Emily L. Pipper). Signed J. M. Brown, Felton Station, Del., Aug. 12, 1867.
people: lecturer on a southern tour (Philadelphian); addressed Sabbath-schools at Wilmington N.C. and the people in the Virginia House of Delegates at Richmond

Names A.M.E. ministers born in Delaware (Anthony Campbell, James Towson, N. C. W. Cannon, Peter D. W. Schureman; of present ministers Bishop Campbell, M. M. Clark, H. J. Young, Geo. Boyer, R. P. articles.headline: Things in Philadelphia (editorial)
articles.summary: The people generally are well and active, now that the extra warm weather is about over. Nearly all have returned from the several watering places and country residences. The churches presented a very slim appearance last Sabbath on account of the camp-meetings. Rev. Theodore Gould is pushing ahead with his mission, and we hope the brethren will receive him with open hearts.
people: minister pushing his mission in Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: Quick Time (editorial account of the Turpin-Murrey wedding)
articles.summary: The editor records a quick trip to and from the wedding of Rev. J. P. Turpin and Miss Murrey of Brooklyn, L.I. Left Philadelphia Tuesday morning, Sept. 3d, at half-past 4 o'clock, accompanied by 'our good brother, Mr. Jones, and wife, and Miss Smith, all of whom reside in Addison street.' Took cars at foot of Walnut street by the Amboy Road; crossed to Brooklyn; the couple were married at about half-past two o'clock in Bridge street A. M. E. church by Rev. Bishop A. W. Wayman; reception at N. H. Lewis' residence in Carroll street, Brooklyn (Rev. N. H. Turpin, father of the groom). Returned to residence in Philadelphia at 10.25 P.M.
people: Bishop who performed the marriage (Rev., Bishop)

articles.author: H. J. Rhodes

Lewis; went to Bensalem; was collecting money to assist in building a church in West Philadelphia, Pa. Describes further travel to New York, Weeksville (Brooklyn) with Mr. J. Dickerson, Bethel church (Sullivan street, N.Y.) and Brother Ross, Saratoga Springs, and Albany (brother and sister Winder), arriving home in Philadelphia.

Born in Baltimore, Md., she removed early in life to Burlington, where she became one of the founders of the A. M. E. articles.headline: Things in Philadelphia (editorial)

Wayman was in the city last Monday and looked remarkably well.

articles.headline: Who Will Be Next? (editorial -- Book Concern fund)

people: of Germantown, Philadelphia; raising funds toward the Book Concern debt (Rev.)

articles.headline: The True Position of the A.M.E. Church of America (editorial)
articles.summary: A long editorial by the Editor (Weaver) stating the position of the African Methodist Episcopal Church: its Methodist faith and government; itinerancy; prayer-, class- and love-feast meetings; the history of its separation from the M.E. Church over slavery and prejudice at the Lord's Table; that 'God put into the heart of our Richard Allen... to make a grand reform,' the body being firmly organized in 1816 with 'African' inserted in the title; its bishops, elders and preachers; perfect equality without distinction of color; and its willingness to reunite with the M.E. Church North on terms of full equality.
people: A.M.E. founder cited as making the 'grand reform'; organized 1816 (historical)

articles.headline: Bishop Campbell and the M.E. Church Controversy
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. Philadelphia, Sept. 16, 1867. On the controversy between some ministers of the M.E. Church and the A.M.E. Church in the Mississippi Valley and Northwest; the presiding Bishop, J. P. Campbell, had been denounced over references to his administration and alleged favoritism to the M.E. Church South. Owing to yellow fever in his field, Campbell came to Philadelphia and, to vindicate himself, the Bishop, Rev. E. Weaver, Rev. John M. Brown, Rev. S. H. Williams and other friends went to the M.E. Preachers' Meeting; Bishop Campbell spoke at length denying he charged the M.E. Church with stealing church property, and recounting a Nashville church bought over the heads of the A.M.E. members. Rev. John W. Brown (imprisoned at New Orleans) was present. M.E. ministers named in text: Dr. Newman (New Orleans Advocate), Brakeman, Knight, Welch, and Mr. Walsh.

articles.headline: Things in Philadelphia (editorial)
articles.summary: On last Sabbath morning we attended Bethel church and heard Bishop Campbell, D.D., preach -- one of the ablest sermons on the subject we have ever listened to; in connection he gave an account of his travels in the South; at the conclusion they gave him nearly forty dollars. At night we attended the Presbyterian church, of which Rev. John B. Reeves is pastor, and heard Mr. Cardozo discourse, giving a very fine account of his work in Charleston, South Carolina, and the educational success there, referring especially to that of Rev. R. H. Cain.

events.name: Book Committee (Committee on Aid for the Book Concern) -- report and division of the $7000 debt
events.description: The Book Committee, having charge of the affairs of the Book Concern in the interval of the General Conference, met July 1, 1867, and recommended raising $7000 to liquidate the present indebtedness of the Book Concern, the Philadelphia Conference having jurisdiction over the Concern during the interval. The whole amount was divided among the districts: Baltimore $1000, Philadelphia $1000, New York $700, New England $800, Ohio $1000, Indiana $700, Missouri $550, Louisiana $350, S. Carolina $550, Georgia $200, Virginia $150, Alabama $125, California $200 (several amounts uncertain on film). Reported 'By order of the Conference.' The accompanying editorial (p.2, 'Let every preacher in the A.M.E. Church read this again and again') appealed to the District Book Stewards -- W. R. Revels (Missouri), W. C. Trevan (Indiana), John Turner (Ohio), Henry Davis (New York), H. M. Turner (Georgia), T. M. D. Ward (California), G. T. Watkins (Virginia), all outside the Philadelphia Conference. Committee member N. H. Turpin is of the New York Conference (Bridge St., Brooklyn) and is left in the text only.
attendees: chairman (Rev.; General Book Steward and Editor)
secretary (Rev.; late editor of the Recorder)

events.description: Notice: the Quarterly Meeting of the Oxford St. Church, Frankford, Philadelphia, to take place Sunday July 14th, at which time the Revs. Wm. Moore, E. Weaver and others will be present. Come one, come all, to the help of the Lord against the mighty. Signed D. P. Seaton, Pastor.

events.description: Editorial ('Rev. events.name: The Philadelphia Conference -- Union Camp Meeting at Media, Pennsylvania
events.description: Report of the Philadelphia Conference Union Camp Meeting at Media, Pa., held the preceding Sabbath (about Sept. 1, 1867); eight or nine thousand persons present. Services: at half-past 6 o'clock Rev. Jacob Mitchell; at half-past 10 o'clock Rev. Wm. Moore; at 3 o'clock Bishop A. W. Wayman (subject 'Eternity,' one of his most powerful sermons); at night Rev. J. B. Hamilton (many came forward to be prayed for and were converted). Editor criticizes the selling of fruit on the Lord's day.
attendees: preached at half-past 10 (Rev.) [identity: one of several Wm. Moores -- as printed]

events.name: Book Committee meeting (A.M.E. Book Concern)
events.description: Notice: The Book Committee will please meet at the Book Rooms on Monday, Sept. 9, at half-past nine o'clock, A.M. No names printed.

events.name: Bishop A. W. Wayman's appointments (Sept.-Oct. 1867)
events.location: Pennsylvania, Delaware, New Jersey, Maryland, Virginia
events.description: Special Notice of Bishop Wayman's appointments: Sun. Sept. 8 Frankford, Pa.; Thu. Sept. 12 Chester, Pa.; Sun. Sept. 15 ordination, Lancaster, Pa.; Tue. Sept. 17 Stroudsburg, Pa.; Sun. Sept. 22 dedication, Laurel, Del.; Mon. night Sept. 23 Sanford(?), Del.; Tue. night Sept. 24 Union Church, Del.; Wed. night Sept. 25 Lock Woods, Del.; Thu. night Sept. 26 Grime's Chapel, Del.; Sun. Sept. 29 dedication, Everal[sham?], N.J.; Sun. Oct. 6 dedication, Royal Oak, Md.; Sun. Oct. 13 dedication, Staunton, Va. Signed A. W. Wayman.
attendees: Bishop whose appointments are listed (Rev., Bishop)

events.name: A.M.E. Book Concern debt assessment on the Annual Conferences ($7,025)
events.description: Special Notice to the members of the Baltimore, Philadelphia, New York, Virginia, South Carolina, Georgia and Florida Annual Conferences. The Philadelphia Conference recommended that $7,025 be raised to relieve the Book Concern debt, proportioned by the Committee of Book Concern: Baltimore Conference ~$1000, Philadelphia $1000, New York $700, Virginia $100, South Carolina $500, Georgia $200, Florida $200. Funds to be raised by the first of October and sent to Rev. E. Weaver, No. 631 Pine street, Philadelphia, or Box 2953. Signed A. W. Wayman.
attendees: Bishop who signed the assessment (Rev., Bishop)
editor/publisher, to receive funds, 631 Pine St. (Rev.)

events.name: Harvest Home and Festival for the Chester A.M.E. Church
events.description: A Harvest Home and Festival at National Hall, Chester, Pa., on Thursday, September 12th, for the benefit of the A.M.E. church at Chester. Exercises: singing and addresses by Bishop Wayman, Revs. E. Weaver, J. Hamilton, D. P. Seaton, Jos. H. Smith, Stephen Smith, and others. Dinner at 1 o'clock (50 cents); festival in the evening (admission 20 cents). Tickets at the office of the Christian Recorder, 631 Pine Street, Phila. Philadelphians can reach Chester via the Baltimore Railroad or the steamer Ariel (Chestnut street wharf 9.45 A.M. and 3.45 P.M.). Jeremiah Young, Pastor.
attendees: pastor of the Chester A.M.E. church (Rev.)

events.name: Macedonia A.M.E. Church, Camden, N.J. -- monthly communion
events.description: Notice: The monthly communion at Macedonia, Sunday, 8th inst., at 3 o'clock, P.M.; the brethren and sisters of sister churches are invited. J. S. Hamilton, Pastor, Camden, N.J., Sept. 7.

events.name: Quarterly Conference appointments (Elder H. Harris in charge)
events.location: Rockingham Mountain, New Hope, Stroudsburg, Attleborough (Pa.)
events.description: Notice: Quarterly Conference at Rockingham Mountain on the 14th and 15th of September; 21st and 22d at New Hope; 28th and 29th at Stroudsburg; October 5th and 6th at Attleborough, Pa. Signed H. Harris(?), Elder in charge.

events.name: Burlington, N.J. Sabbath-school Picnic and Temperance Meeting
events.description: Notice: A grand Sabbath-school Picnic at Burlington, N.J., on the 12th of September, 1867, in the grove; a Temperance Meeting the same evening in the church; refreshments of all kinds. Jacob Mitchell, Pastor.

events.name: Harvest Home -- Green's Tabernacle No. 6, I.O. of B. & S. of Love and Charity, Woodbury, N.J.
events.description: Green's Tabernacle, No. 6, I.O. of B. & S. (Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters) of Love and Charity, will hold a Harvest Home at Woodbury, N.J., Sept. 19, 1867. Cars leave upper Ferry, Market Street; stage from Gloucester. No individual names printed.

events.name: Macedonia A.M.E. Church, Camden, N.J. -- Quarterly Meeting
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Macedonia, Sunday, September 22d. Love-feast in the morning at 8 1/2 o'clock. Preaching: at 11 o'clock Rev. Wm. Moore; at 3 o'clock Rev. D. Dorrell; at 8 o'clock Rev. G. E. Boyer. J. B. Hamilton, Pastor. Camden, N.J., September 10, 1867.

events.name: New Brunswick Mount Zion A.M.E. Church -- Quarterly Meeting and grand rally
events.location: Mount Zion A.M.E. Church, New Brunswick, New Jersey
events.description: Two notices: the Second Quarterly Meeting for New Brunswick Mount Zion A.M.E. Church on the First Sunday in October (6th), expecting Sister Mrs. Williams from Trenton and Rev. R. F. Wayman; and a second grand rally on the Second Sunday in October (13th). Wm. H. Williams, Minister-in-Charge.
attendees: minister-in-charge, New Brunswick Mount Zion A.M.E. (Rev.)

events.name: Evesham Mount, N.J. -- new church dedication and Quarterly Conference
events.description: The dedication of the new church at Evesham Mount, N.J., on Sunday, September 29th; the Quarterly Meeting the same day; Quarterly Conference on the 28th at 12 o'clock M. Bishop Wayman, Rev. W. Moore and others will be present. Rev. Jacob Mitchell, Pastor. September 14.

events.name: Quarterly Meeting at Mount Holly, N.J.
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Mount Holly, on Sunday, October 6th. September 14. No names printed.

events.name: Quarterly Meeting at Burlington, N.J.
events.description: Quarterly Meeting at Burlington, N.J., on Sabbath, October 13th. Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, Pastor. September 14.

events.name: New A.M.E. Church, Smyrna, Del. -- corner-stone laying
events.description: The corner-stone for the new A.M.E. Church, Smyrna, Del., will be laid on Thursday, Sept. 19th, by Bishop Wayman. H. H. Lewis, Pastor. September 14.
attendees: Bishop, to lay the corner-stone (Rev., Bishop)

events.name: New A.M.E. Church, Stroudsburg, Pa. -- corner-stone laying
events.description: The corner-stone for the new A.M.E. Church, Stroudsburg, Pa., will be laid on Tuesday, Sept. 17, by Bishop Wayman. R. Barney, Pastor. September 14.
attendees: Bishop, to lay the corner-stone (Rev., Bishop)

events.name: Roll of Honor -- collections received per Theodore Gould, Agent
events.description: Sums received for the Roll of Honor per Theodore Gould, Agent. Bridgeton, N.J.: Mr. J. Gould $6.75; Mr. J. Cuff $6.00; Miss Isabella Wright 75c; Miss M. Black 62c; Mr. Charles Griffin 50c. Salem, N.J.: Mr. J. Pennelton $1.90; Miss Carolina Lee 50c; Mrs. E. A. Lee 50c; Hannah A. Roberts $1.30; Mr. Samuel Johnson $1.00; Mrs. E. Jasper $2.05; Miss D. Wilson $1.15. Woodbury, N.J.: Mrs. Amelia Anderson $1.05. (New Jersey donor list; individual names given in description only.)
attendees: agent who forwarded the Roll of Honor collections

events.name: Grand Concert at the Cherry Street Baptist Church
events.description: On the 26th inst. a grand concert will be given at the Cherry Street Baptist church, of which Rev. Theodore D. Miller is the accredited pastor. Expected to be one of the greatest ever given in Philadelphia. Performers: Miss E. S. Greenfield, the celebrated Black Swan, and troupe; also Mrs. Mary L. Brown, Mr. A. Buchman, and several other first-class performers.

events.name: Rev. Isaiah Hunkerson, of Wesley, to address the citizens of Philadelphia
events.description: N.B. -- Rev. Isaiah Hunkerson/Honkerson (surname uncertain even at high resolution), of Wesley, will address the citizens of Philadelphia on the 28th inst. 'We hope that he will have a full house.' (A brief editorial P.S.) The minister's surname is left in the text only -- not linked -- because the reading is uncertain.

events.name: A Statement -- Committee of the Union Camp Meeting of the Philadelphia District (Media)
events.description: The Committee of the Union Camp Meeting of the Philadelphia District thank the people of Philadelphia and of the vicinity of Media. The meeting ran August 24 to September 8, 1867, embracing one Sabbath, notable for Bishop Wayman's sermon on 'Eternity'; not less than 15,000 people on the ground and no disorder. Committee: Rev. D. Dorrell, Rev. William Moore, Rev. G. E. Boyer, Rev. D. P. Seaton, Rev. H. J. Rhodes, Rev. J. B. Hamilton, Rev. Jacob Mitchell, Rev. J. Young, Rev. W. Williams.

events.name: Bishop Campbell to preach at Bethel and Union churches
events.location: Bethel Church (South Sixth St. below Pine) and Union Church (Coates St. below Fifth), Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: Bishop Campbell will preach at Bethel Church, South Sixth street, below Pine, at 10 o'clock A.M., and Union church, Coates Street, below Fifth, at 7 1/2 P.M., next Sabbath, Sept. 22d, 1867.
attendees: Bishop, preaching at Bethel and Union (Rev., Bishop)

events.name: Missionary meeting addressed by Rev. John M. Brown at Wesley church
events.description: Personal: Rev. John M. Brown addressed a missionary meeting, on the 19th instant, at Wesley church. There was not a very large attendance, but those present did what they could for the cause of missions.

events.name: Reception of Gen. Phil. Sheridan in Philadelphia (procession)
events.location: Baltimore & Philadelphia Depot to the Continental Hotel (via Arch and Twelfth streets), Philadelphia
events.description: General Sheridan arrived at the Baltimore and Philadelphia Depot on Wednesday evening, Sept. 25; the largest crowd ever seen in Philadelphia assembled from the depot to Arch street and along Twelfth to the Continental Hotel. Portions of the grand army of the Potomac, white and colored, paraded, and the fire companies turned out. The General rode in an open barouche, accompanied by Mayor McMichael. (Parade with colored troops; no Black individuals named.)

events.name: Laying of the corner-stone of the A.M.E. Church, Carlisle, Pa.
events.description: Procession formed at 2 o'clock on Centre Square. Order of procession: Bishop Wayman; Rev. Amos Wilson, pastor; ministers of the different denominations; the Douglass Equal Rights League of Carlisle; a detachment of colored soldiers from the Barracks; Freemasons from Harrisburg and other places; led by a drum corps. Bishop Wayman gave out the hymn and delivered the address; prayer by Rev. Wm. H. Keith (white) of the M.E. Church. Articles deposited in the corner-stone: the Bible, Discipline, Hymn Book, Apostles' Creed, Minutes of the Baltimore Conference, Christian Recorder dated Aug. 17, 1867, and names of the President, Governor of Pennsylvania, minister in charge, Trustees and Building Committee. The minister's call was for $200.
attendees: Bishop, laid the corner-stone and gave the address (Rev., Bishop)

events.name: Thanks for a festival of the Lancaster City, Pa. charge
events.description: A card of thanks (to the Editor): the minister thanks the young ladies and gentlemen of his charge in Lancaster City, Pa., and especially the young ladies of the committee, who presented him with $11.40, the proceeds of a festival held on the 4th of September, 1867. Committee: Misses Catharine Johnson, Anna Moore, Mary Morris, and Mrs. Harriet West. James V. Pierce, Minister.
attendees: minister of the Lancaster City, Pa. charge (Rev.)
